summary: I intransitive growth in body condition contrasts with the III causative used by livestock dealers. The new III example has a plural patient suffix -nne and an implied agent established by the preceding trading account.
The Part act. describes fat/plump states with masculine singular, feminine singular and plural forms. It need not assert an event of having become fat in each context.

Permitted lookup distinguishes tqn 2 II mtaqən 'stecken' and tyqn 'glauben'; neither explains lean animals being fattened before resale. No etymology is inferred for the new stem beyond its relation to the existing root.
Confirm the III singular base forms from native speakers; only matəqnənne is present here, so no Preterit is reconstructed.
Does taqine of grain ears specifically mean plump/full rather than firm? The contrast with a thin ear supports fullness, but one dream context cannot settle narrower lexical distinctions.
Part act. taqine extends plumpness to ears of grain in Joseph's dream, contrasted with zaʕīf. Human fattening in 87/95 likewise preserves the literal body-condition meaning.
